OTP input

A one-time code, one box per character, posted as one field. Every box is drawn from the input’s own recipe.

The boxes carry no name. A hidden input carries the joined code, so the form posts code=482193 and nothing else. Typing, pasting and the browser’s autofill need the package’s script; the gallery loads none, so what is here is the server’s render.

Copy button

A ds::button that copies a value and confirms in place. Both labels sit in one cell from the first paint, so the button is as wide as “Copied” before anything is pressed and never jumps.

Copying needs the package’s script; the gallery loads none, so these are the server’s render, at rest. A refused clipboard changes nothing on the button and dispatches copy-failed instead.

Rating

Stars that are radios underneath: one name, one value posted, the arrow keys and the form’s required check for free. Hovering previews “up to here” and leaving restores the choice, all in CSS. Readonly is one image, named “4.5 out of 5”.

No script at all. The faint cross after the stars is “No rating”, the way back once a star is chosen; it is transparent while it is itself the choice, and omitted when the rating is required.

Chip group

Pressable filters. Each chip is a real radio or checkbox under a pill, so the group posts with the form and binds with wire:model on the group. Or each is a link, for filtering by URL. A chosen chip opens a check before its words, by a width transition, so the row slides rather than jumps.

No script. ds::badge is the static pill; this is the one you press. A group is all inputs or all links, never both, and says so when the view renders.

Segmented control

One of a few views or modes, side by side in a track. Each segment is a real radio, so the control posts with the form, takes the arrow keys and binds with wire:model on the control. Or each is a link, for switching views by URL.

No script needed. With the package's script and Alpine, one highlight slides between segments; this page loads no Alpine, so what you see is the face CSS draws on the chosen segment, which is also what every page shows before the script runs.

Toolbar

A row of tools that is one stop in the tab order: the arrow keys move between its buttons, Home and End jump to the ends. With the script, a highlight follows the pointer and the keyboard from button to button, and darkens while one is pressed.

Radio cards

Options big enough to compare: plans, shipping methods. The whole card is the label of a real, visible radio, so the arrow keys, required and posting are the browser’s. The chosen card is ringed by :has(:checked); no ring slides between them.

No script. The name a screen reader hears is the title and the meta (“Pro, $12 a month”); the description and body are read after it. Every column count collapses to one on a phone.

Tag input

Short values typed into a field and kept as removable chips. Each chip carries the hidden input it posts, so what is on screen and what is submitted cannot disagree.

An entry that cannot be added stays in the box with a message under it, in the help line’s place. Nothing typed is ever dropped. The gallery loads no script, so the chips here are the server’s.

Number field

A native type=number with decrease and increase buttons. The arrow keys and typing are the browser’s; the buttons add a press, a hold that repeats, and a stop at each bound.

The buttons are out of the tab order on purpose: a keyboard already has the arrow keys. A button at its bound is disabled by the server’s render, before any script runs.

Password: reveal and strength

reveal on ds::input adds a show/hide toggle; ds::password-strength is a meter bound to the field by its id. The score is a hint for the person typing, not a security control.

The level is spoken in words through a polite live region and shown by how many bars are lit, never by colour alone. The gallery loads no script, so the meter here is empty; the documentation image shows it scored.

The active underline is fg, not accent. A tab row is structure, not a link — colouring the active one accent makes the inactive tabs look like the links.

Toast

Surface with a border, not the alert’s tinted wash: it floats over unknown content and has to paint an opaque ground. The tone lives in the icon alone, so four stacked toasts do not become a colour chart.

The region is rendered always, and empty most of the time. A live region only announces content that arrives after it is in the document — render it with the first toast and the first toast is silent.

Switch

A setting that takes effect. role="switch" makes a screen reader say “on” and “off” — “unchecked”, for a setting that is simply off, reads as a form the reader failed to fill in.

The label sits left and the control right, the opposite of the checkbox: a switch is one of a list of settings the reader scans down the left edge.

Accordion

Sections that expand one at a time. The one component in the system that holds state — exclusivity is a relationship between items, so no single item can enforce it.

A collapsed panel is visibility: hidden, not overflow: hidden. That takes its content out of the tab order AND the accessibility tree; a collapsed section whose links are still tabbable is the classic broken accordion, and it looks perfect.
Exclusive · the open section renders open, before Alpine boots

Combobox

A select with a text filter. multiple is a mode of it, not a second component — chips and aria-multiselectable are the whole difference.

Chips sit inside the field. A list of choices below the control reads as results, and people click them expecting to select rather than to remove.

Date picker

A calendar for one date or a range. Every value is a Y-m-d string, never a Date — new Date('2026-03-29') is UTC midnight, which west of Greenwich is the 28th.

A range posts two fields. Two dates are two values, and squeezing them into one string means every consumer writing the same parser.
Range · endpoints inverse, the span washed — shown open

File upload

A styled file field with drag-and-drop and local previews. It does not upload anything — progress needs somewhere to upload to, and that is a backend contract nothing else here has.

The real <input type="file"> is stretched over the whole zone at zero opacity, so the entire area is the control and drag-and-drop lands on the element that owns the files.
